scope: Isolated cache, native page-coverage and durable checkpoint qualification
native_pdf_assertions: Every inspected page is inventoried in order
Exact unique native page text survives full forward and reversed requests
Reading after bounded 512-entry cache eviction retains complete request-owned results
additional_cases: 1001-page original is rejected by the default inspection limit without modification
1000-page durable inventory survives SQLite reopen and caller-side mutations
LRU access order, replacement and TTL expiry
Document identity isolation and copied page return values
Missing-page and interrupted-reader retries preserve committed cache entries without false success
Four concurrent callers retain complete results during shared cache eviction
Legacy translation cache isolates language direction and domain without network calls
Target, domain, jurisdiction and glossary changes reject stale translation checkpoints
Restart invalidates old attempts; a new model revision publishes once and duplicate checkpoint is rejected
audit_findings: Legacy native reader uses request-owned dictionaries independent of its bounded LRU
The current review pipeline does not have an inference-result cache; it uses durable document/page revisions and job attempts
Context and glossary changes invalidate approvals and reject old result publication
Local model manifests and files are verified separately by existing model integrity tests
limitations: Synthetic native text documents only; no scan recognition accuracy measurement
Direct native inspection and extraction; no bounded worker or live HTTP server invoked
Durable translation publication uses synthetic results, not model inference
This is not a full 1000-page OCR, translation, human-review or export workload
Broader contextual translation and bilingual quality remain separate qualification work
isolation: All test PDFs and SQLite workspaces are in pytest tmp_path; no backend/local-data, user uploads, network requests, deployment or server restart
